candidates.title: Comment la justice climatique risque de devenir un instrument de domination : le cas du Just Energy Transition Partnerships (JETP) au Sénégal

peer_reviewed.evidence: HAL field peerReviewing_s=0; venue is The Conversation France, a general-audience outlet

candidates.abstract_excerpt: C'est un projet à 2,5 milliards d'euros qui se réclame de la justice climatique. [...] quand on regarde la nature des fonds et le contexte géopolitique, une question reste en suspens : ce mécanisme n'entretient-il pas les inégalités actuelles ?
candidates.why: Journalistic essay raising a domination/inequality framing close in spirit to P3/P4, but no economic analysis of balance sheets, aggregate governance, or strategic refusal. Known control piece; does not preempt any proposition on its own peer-reviewed merits since it is not peer-reviewed.

candidates.title: Exceptions for stop building coal-fired power plants in Indonesia

peer_reviewed.evidence: E3S Web of Conferences is a conference-proceedings series with light/varying review; not a peer-reviewed journal in the strict sense

candidates.abstract_excerpt: Indonesia employed rhetorical commitments to secure international renewable energy funding while using coal plant allowances as 'bargaining positions' in global forums. The country secured $20 billion from G7 countries through the Just Energy Transition Partnership scheme [...] strategically leveraged coal infrastructure discussions to attract climate transition investments.
candidates.why: Closest thing found to a preemption of P3 (agentivité stratégique / détournement vers agenda propre, notamment charbon): argues Indonesia used coal continuation as a bargaining chip to extract JETP funds. But framed as opportunistic negotiation tactic, pre-dates the finalized CIPP, and is conference-proceedings tier, not a full peer-reviewed economic analysis of strategic refusal/redirection as P3 frames it.

candidates.title: Discursive Hegemonic Mediation dalam Pemberitaan Media tentang Just Energy Transition Partnership (JETP) di Indonesia: Analisis Wacana Kritis Model Fairclough

peer_reviewed.evidence: OJS-format Indonesian academic journal; peer-review workflow not independently verified (site not directly accessible in this pass)

candidates.abstract_excerpt: global dominance is reproduced through the normalization of dependency and the limitation of critical perspectives within policy narratives [...] media outlets amplify narratives about green investment while downplaying structural concerns regarding loans versus grants [...] JETP's legitimacy in Indonesia is discursively constructed through processes that normalize dependency.
candidates.why: The single closest finding of this whole pass to P1: explicitly names the loans-versus-grants structural concern and a dependency-normalization critique. But it is a critical-discourse-analysis (Fairclough) study of MEDIA FRAMING, not a balance-sheet/DSA/operator-insolvency economic analysis. It documents that the loan/grant asymmetry is publicly under-discussed in Indonesian media — which is adjacent to, but does not perform, the P1 argument.

candidates.title: Implementation of Just Energy Transition Partnership (JETP) Indonesia

peer_reviewed.evidence: OJS-format Indonesian academic journal; review workflow not independently verified

candidates.abstract_excerpt: most financing is loan-based, which increases Indonesia's fiscal burden while contributing little to renewable deployment [...] the partnership risks creating technological and financial dependency rather than fostering genuine energy independence.
candidates.why: Second-closest finding to P1: states plainly that JETP financing is loan-heavy and raises Indonesia's fiscal burden. Stops short of the granular balance-sheet mechanics of P1 (sovereign debt ceilings/DSA thresholds, PLN operator insolvency under repressed tariffs, FX exposure, cost of capital) — it is a fiscal-burden/dependency claim at a general policy-analysis level, not a quantified balance-sheet argument.

candidates.title: Indonesia's Energy Security Strategy through the Just Energy Transition Partnership: Implications for Energy Sovereignty

peer_reviewed.evidence: OJS-format Indonesian academic journal; review workflow not independently verified

candidates.abstract_excerpt: while JETP partially strengthens energy sovereignty through sector diversification and transition capacity, Indonesia's energy system remained reliant on fossil fuels and imports by 2024 [...] JETP 'shifts dependence towards external capital and technological networks', resulting in only partial strengthening of energy security.
candidates.why: Positive-control piece. Uses Cherp & Jewell energy-sovereignty framework, finds JETP substitutes one dependency (fossil imports) for another (external capital/technology) — thematically adjacent to P4's solvency/agentivity trade-off, but argued through sovereignty theory, not the solvency-distribution logic of P4.

candidates.title: International Collaboration and Coordination Vietnam's Energy Transition: The Role of International Partners Through the Just Energy Transition Partnership

peer_reviewed.evidence: OJS-format Indonesian academic journal; review workflow not independently verified

candidates.abstract_excerpt: collaboration operates through the Resource Mobilisation Plan governance structure, sector reforms, and renewable energy initiatives [...] institutionalized multilateralism, in which Vietnam's national interests and global climate mitigation objectives are aligned.
candidates.why: Positive-control piece. Describes the coordination mechanism (Resource Mobilisation Plan) in positive terms; if anything it is mild counter-evidence to P2's 'no one has a mandate to assess the aggregate' claim by describing a coordination structure — though the RMP as commonly understood is a country-side planning document, not a joint solvency assessment by donors, so it does not actually preempt P2. Flagged for the author's own judgment.

verdict: Aucune préemption peer-reviewed nette de P1, P2, P3 ou P4 trouvée dans les canaux non anglophones sondés. Les deux trouvailles les plus proches sont indonésiennes et de 2026 : (1) Robertua et al. 2026 (Global Political Studies Journal) — analyse de discours critique qui nomme explicitement le déséquilibre prêts/dons et une 'normalisation de la dépendance', adjacent à P1 mais par la voie du discours médiatique, pas du bilan économique ; (2) Rizqia & Wulansari 2026 (Jurnal Manajemen dan Bisnis Madani) — affirme que le financement à dominante prêt alourdit le fardeau budgétaire indonésien, adjacent à P1 mais sans la mécanique de bilan détaillée (plafond de dette, DSA, insolvabilité PLN, change). Aucune trouvaille n'aborde frontalement P2 (gouvernance de l'agrégat, 'jointly announced severally owed') ni P4 (la solvabilité achète l'agentivité) ; Andriko et al. 2023 (E3S Web of Conferences, article de congrès) est la seule pièce touchant P3 (détournement stratégique du paquet vers le maintien du charbon comme levier de négociation), mais avec une portée et un statut de publication modestes. VERDICT MITIGÉ, pas un verdict propre : plusieurs canaux à fort risque documenté (Cairn, Garuda, Neliti direct, AFD, Ferdi, Enda Energie, Wuppertal, adelphi, GIZ) sont restés INACCESSIBLES sous les contraintes d'outillage de cette passe (DNS, 403, 404, budget WebSearch épuisé, OpenAlex à 429 pendant ~10h) — leur silence ne doit PAS être lu comme une absence confirmée. Le contrôle positif HAL a réussi et confirmé le piège documenté (tribune non peer-reviewed). Les deux contrôles positifs indonésiens ont réussi via Crossref (substitut aux portails directs, eux-mêmes bloqués). Recommandation : une repasse ultérieure devrait retenter Cairn/Garuda/Neliti/AFD/Ferdi/Enda Energie avec un outil d'accès web différent (navigateur authentifié ou proxy) avant de considérer ces canaux comme réellement secs.
